app: the source world Biome Location Library
source_readme:
# the source world Biomes JSON Split

Generated from: `the source world_Immersive_Locations_Google_Doc.docx`

This ZIP contains the requested folder tree:

`biomes/<Biome Category>/<Requested Biome>/<capital|city|town|village>/*.json`

Counts:

- Original DOCX source sections detected: 52
- Requested target biome folders: 17
- Target JSON files created: 68
- Original source JSON archive files created: 52

Each requested biome folder has four filled settlement subfolders: `capital`, `city`, `town`, and `village`.

Some requested biome names did not exist as exact source headings in the DOCX, so the JSON includes a `mapping.mapping_note` explaining which original biome profile was used as the closest source. To make sure no original DOCX content is lost, every original source section is also preserved under `original_source_sections/`.

Main files:

- `manifest.json` — full inventory and mapping table.
- `biomes/` — requested folder tree.
- `original_source_sections/` — exact original section JSON archive from the DOCX.

entries.biome_identity: timber halls, herbal markets, bowyers, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, hunting lodges, and canopy ropeways.
strict_placement_rules: Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.

Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.

Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

mapping.mapping_note: Directly mapped to Forest; emphasize timber halls, herbal markets, hunting lodges, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, bowyers, and canopy ropeways.

content.summary: Prestigious, extravagant, exotic, heavily regulated, and expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.

content.biome_specific_section_title: Forest Biome-Specific Goods and Services
content.full_raw_text:
Capital City - Forest
Source file: Capital_City_Forest.html
Prestigious, extravagant, exotic, heavily regulated, and expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: timber halls, herbal markets, bowyers, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, hunting lodges, and canopy ropeways.
Market structure: grand bazaars, embassy hostels, luxury hotels, master guild courts, royal hospitals, relic vaults, and regulated portal offices. Elite purchases include tiny plated courses, rare materials, signed masterwork goods, and private appointments.
Availability rule: Capitals have the broadest stock, elite appointments, rare goods, and strict records for dangerous goods.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office; Skyship Station; Portal Network Building
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

sections.title: Strict Placement Rules
raw_lines: • Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.

• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.

• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

content.biome_specific_section_title: Forest Biome-Specific Goods and Services
content.full_raw_text:
City - Forest
Source file: City_Forest.html
Broad, crowded, specialized, fashionable, and more expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: timber halls, herbal markets, bowyers, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, hunting lodges, and canopy ropeways.
Market structure: district markets, guild halls, hotels, armory rows, hospitals, restaurants, bazaars, and licensed arcane counters. Fine goods, rare goods, and commissioned masterwork services are common.
Availability rule: Cities have full permanent districts; almost every listed item can be purchased without waiting unless it is restricted.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office; Skyship Station; Portal Network Building
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

DM Use Notes
Use these tables as the settlement shopping floor. The same item always has a designated location, so players know where to go and what kind of scene they are entering. Increase or decrease stock by neighborhood, danger rating, scarcity, guild politics, holy days, blockades, monster pressure, or local corruption.
All names are plain English except setting terms such as thundercoil. Merge notes and audit wording have been removed from this player-facing version.

entries.biome_identity: timber halls, herbal markets, bowyers, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, hunting lodges, and canopy ropeways.
strict_placement_rules: Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.

Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.

Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

content.biome_specific_section_title: Forest Biome-Specific Goods and Services
content.full_raw_text:
Town - Forest
Source file: Town_Forest.html
Fair-priced, varied, reliable, and built for locals plus travelers shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: timber halls, herbal markets, bowyers, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, hunting lodges, and canopy ropeways.
Market structure: town market square, guild street, stable yard, tavern row, clinic, smithy, and craft halls. Luxury goods are available in small batches or by commission.
Availability rule: Towns have permanent shops for most goods, with rare and masterwork goods handled by guild commission.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

Use these tables as the settlement shopping floor. The same item always has a designated location, so players know where to go and what kind of scene they are entering. Increase or decrease stock by neighborhood, danger rating, scarcity, guild politics, holy days, blockades, monster pressure, or local corruption.

entries.biome_identity: timber halls, herbal markets, bowyers, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, hunting lodges, and canopy ropeways.
strict_placement_rules: Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.

Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.

Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

mapping.mapping_note: Directly mapped to Forest; emphasize timber halls, herbal markets, hunting lodges, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, bowyers, and canopy ropeways.

content.summary: Cheap, practical, hearty, local, and generous shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.

content.biome_specific_section_title: Forest Biome-Specific Goods and Services
content.full_raw_text:
Village - Forest
Source file: Village_Forest.html
Cheap, practical, hearty, local, and generous shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: timber halls, herbal markets, bowyers, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, hunting lodges, and canopy ropeways.
Market structure: small common market, hearth inn, livery yard, herb counter, smith stall, and traveling peddlers. Rare luxury goods require ordering through a caravan factor.
Availability rule: Villages list the same categories so the DM has a designated place for every purchase, but rare items are special orders, traveling-stall stock, shrine stock, or one-at-a-time commissions.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

Use these tables as the settlement shopping floor. The same item always has a designated location, so players know where to go and what kind of scene they are entering. Increase or decrease stock by neighborhood, danger rating, scarcity, guild politics, holy days, blockades, monster pressure, or local corruption.
All names are plain English except setting terms such as thundercoil. Merge notes and audit wording have been removed from this player-facing version.

entries.biome_identity: stilt markets, poleboat rentals, peat fires, reed houses, leech doctors, mosquito-net inns, and marsh guide camps.
strict_placement_rules: Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.

Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.

Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

content.summary: Prestigious, extravagant, exotic, heavily regulated, and expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.

content.full_raw_text:
Capital City - Swamp Marsh
Source file: Capital_City_Swamp_Marsh.html
Prestigious, extravagant, exotic, heavily regulated, and expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: stilt markets, poleboat rentals, peat fires, reed houses, leech doctors, mosquito-net inns, and marsh guide camps.
Market structure: grand bazaars, embassy hostels, luxury hotels, master guild courts, royal hospitals, relic vaults, and regulated portal offices. Elite purchases include tiny plated courses, rare materials, signed masterwork goods, and private appointments.
Availability rule: Capitals have the broadest stock, elite appointments, rare goods, and strict records for dangerous goods.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office; Skyship Station; Portal Network Building
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

entries.biome_identity: stilt markets, poleboat rentals, peat fires, reed houses, leech doctors, mosquito-net inns, and marsh guide camps.
strict_placement_rules: Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.

Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.

Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

content.summary: Broad, crowded, specialized, fashionable, and more expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.

content.full_raw_text:
City - Swamp Marsh
Source file: City_Swamp_Marsh.html
Broad, crowded, specialized, fashionable, and more expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: stilt markets, poleboat rentals, peat fires, reed houses, leech doctors, mosquito-net inns, and marsh guide camps.
Market structure: district markets, guild halls, hotels, armory rows, hospitals, restaurants, bazaars, and licensed arcane counters. Fine goods, rare goods, and commissioned masterwork services are common.
Availability rule: Cities have full permanent districts; almost every listed item can be purchased without waiting unless it is restricted.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office; Skyship Station; Portal Network Building
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

content.full_raw_text:
Town - Swamp Marsh
Source file: Town_Swamp_Marsh.html
Fair-priced, varied, reliable, and built for locals plus travelers shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: stilt markets, poleboat rentals, peat fires, reed houses, leech doctors, mosquito-net inns, and marsh guide camps.
Market structure: town market square, guild street, stable yard, tavern row, clinic, smithy, and craft halls. Luxury goods are available in small batches or by commission.
Availability rule: Towns have permanent shops for most goods, with rare and masterwork goods handled by guild commission.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

content.biome_specific_section_title: Swamp Marsh Biome-Specific Goods and Services
content.full_raw_text:
Village - Swamp Marsh
Source file: Village_Swamp_Marsh.html
Cheap, practical, hearty, local, and generous shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: stilt markets, poleboat rentals, peat fires, reed houses, leech doctors, mosquito-net inns, and marsh guide camps.
Market structure: small common market, hearth inn, livery yard, herb counter, smith stall, and traveling peddlers. Rare luxury goods require ordering through a caravan factor.
Availability rule: Villages list the same categories so the DM has a designated place for every purchase, but rare items are special orders, traveling-stall stock, shrine stock, or one-at-a-time commissions.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

DM Use Notes
Use these tables as the settlement shopping floor. The same item always has a designated location, so players know where to go and what kind of scene they are entering. Increase or decrease stock by neighborhood, danger rating, scarcity, guild politics, holy days, blockades, monster pressure, or local corruption.
All names are plain English except setting terms such as thundercoil. Merge notes and audit wording have been removed from this player-facing version.

entries.biome_identity: timber halls, herbal markets, bowyers, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, hunting lodges, and canopy ropeways.
strict_placement_rules: Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.

Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.

Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

content.biome_specific_section_title: Forest Biome-Specific Goods and Services
content.full_raw_text:
Capital City - Forest
Source file: Capital_City_Forest.html
Prestigious, extravagant, exotic, heavily regulated, and expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: timber halls, herbal markets, bowyers, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, hunting lodges, and canopy ropeways.
Market structure: grand bazaars, embassy hostels, luxury hotels, master guild courts, royal hospitals, relic vaults, and regulated portal offices. Elite purchases include tiny plated courses, rare materials, signed masterwork goods, and private appointments.
Availability rule: Capitals have the broadest stock, elite appointments, rare goods, and strict records for dangerous goods.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office; Skyship Station; Portal Network Building
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

DM Use Notes
Use these tables as the settlement shopping floor. The same item always has a designated location, so players know where to go and what kind of scene they are entering. Increase or decrease stock by neighborhood, danger rating, scarcity, guild politics, holy days, blockades, monster pressure, or local corruption.
All names are plain English except setting terms such as thundercoil. Merge notes and audit wording have been removed from this player-facing version.

entries.biome_identity: timber halls, herbal markets, bowyers, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, hunting lodges, and canopy ropeways.
strict_placement_rules: Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.

Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.

Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

mapping.mapping_note: Mapped to Forest; for partial-forest generation, blend woodland services with more open settlement districts.

content.summary: Broad, crowded, specialized, fashionable, and more expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.

content.biome_specific_section_title: Forest Biome-Specific Goods and Services
content.full_raw_text:
City - Forest
Source file: City_Forest.html
Broad, crowded, specialized, fashionable, and more expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: timber halls, herbal markets, bowyers, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, hunting lodges, and canopy ropeways.
Market structure: district markets, guild halls, hotels, armory rows, hospitals, restaurants, bazaars, and licensed arcane counters. Fine goods, rare goods, and commissioned masterwork services are common.
Availability rule: Cities have full permanent districts; almost every listed item can be purchased without waiting unless it is restricted.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office; Skyship Station; Portal Network Building
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

DM Use Notes
Use these tables as the settlement shopping floor. The same item always has a designated location, so players know where to go and what kind of scene they are entering. Increase or decrease stock by neighborhood, danger rating, scarcity, guild politics, holy days, blockades, monster pressure, or local corruption.
All names are plain English except setting terms such as thundercoil. Merge notes and audit wording have been removed from this player-facing version.

entries.biome_identity: timber halls, herbal markets, bowyers, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, hunting lodges, and canopy ropeways.
strict_placement_rules: Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.

Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.

Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

mapping.mapping_note: Mapped to Forest; for partial-forest generation, blend woodland services with more open settlement districts.

content.summary: Fair-priced, varied, reliable, and built for locals plus travelers shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.

content.biome_specific_section_title: Forest Biome-Specific Goods and Services
content.full_raw_text:
Town - Forest
Source file: Town_Forest.html
Fair-priced, varied, reliable, and built for locals plus travelers shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: timber halls, herbal markets, bowyers, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, hunting lodges, and canopy ropeways.
Market structure: town market square, guild street, stable yard, tavern row, clinic, smithy, and craft halls. Luxury goods are available in small batches or by commission.
Availability rule: Towns have permanent shops for most goods, with rare and masterwork goods handled by guild commission.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

entries.biome_identity: timber halls, herbal markets, bowyers, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, hunting lodges, and canopy ropeways.
strict_placement_rules: Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.

Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.

Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

mapping.mapping_note: Mapped to Forest; for partial-forest generation, blend woodland services with more open settlement districts.

content.summary: Cheap, practical, hearty, local, and generous shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.

content.full_raw_text:
Village - Forest
Source file: Village_Forest.html
Cheap, practical, hearty, local, and generous shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: timber halls, herbal markets, bowyers, woodland inns, mushroom cellars, hunting lodges, and canopy ropeways.
Market structure: small common market, hearth inn, livery yard, herb counter, smith stall, and traveling peddlers. Rare luxury goods require ordering through a caravan factor.
Availability rule: Villages list the same categories so the DM has a designated place for every purchase, but rare items are special orders, traveling-stall stock, shrine stock, or one-at-a-time commissions.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

content.full_raw_text:
Capital City - Rainforest
Source file: Capital_City_Rainforest.html
Prestigious, extravagant, exotic, heavily regulated, and expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: canopy markets, covered walkways, medicinal gardens, insect-screen hostels, river skiffs, resin craft shops, and storm shelters.
Market structure: grand bazaars, embassy hostels, luxury hotels, master guild courts, royal hospitals, relic vaults, and regulated portal offices. Elite purchases include tiny plated courses, rare materials, signed masterwork goods, and private appointments.
Availability rule: Capitals have the broadest stock, elite appointments, rare goods, and strict records for dangerous goods.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office; Skyship Station; Portal Network Building
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules

Use these tables as the settlement shopping floor. The same item always has a designated location, so players know where to go and what kind of scene they are entering. Increase or decrease stock by neighborhood, danger rating, scarcity, guild politics, holy days, blockades, monster pressure, or local corruption.

content.biome_specific_section_title: Rainforest Biome-Specific Goods and Services
content.full_raw_text:
City - Rainforest
Source file: City_Rainforest.html
Broad, crowded, specialized, fashionable, and more expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: canopy markets, covered walkways, medicinal gardens, insect-screen hostels, river skiffs, resin craft shops, and storm shelters.
Market structure: district markets, guild halls, hotels, armory rows, hospitals, restaurants, bazaars, and licensed arcane counters. Fine goods, rare goods, and commissioned masterwork services are common.
Availability rule: Cities have full permanent districts; almost every listed item can be purchased without waiting unless it is restricted.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office; Skyship Station; Portal Network Building
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

DM Use Notes
Use these tables as the settlement shopping floor. The same item always has a designated location, so players know where to go and what kind of scene they are entering. Increase or decrease stock by neighborhood, danger rating, scarcity, guild politics, holy days, blockades, monster pressure, or local corruption.
All names are plain English except setting terms such as thundercoil. Merge notes and audit wording have been removed from this player-facing version.

entries.biome_identity: canopy markets, covered walkways, medicinal gardens, insect-screen hostels, river skiffs, resin craft shops, and storm shelters.
strict_placement_rules: Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.

Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.

Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

mapping.mapping_note: Mapped to Rainforest because it contains canopy markets, covered walkways, medicinal gardens, river skiffs, resin craft shops, and storm shelters; use vertical treehouse/canopy flavor.

content.summary: Fair-priced, varied, reliable, and built for locals plus travelers shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.

content.biome_specific_section_title: Rainforest Biome-Specific Goods and Services
content.full_raw_text:
Town - Rainforest
Source file: Town_Rainforest.html
Fair-priced, varied, reliable, and built for locals plus travelers shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: canopy markets, covered walkways, medicinal gardens, insect-screen hostels, river skiffs, resin craft shops, and storm shelters.
Market structure: town market square, guild street, stable yard, tavern row, clinic, smithy, and craft halls. Luxury goods are available in small batches or by commission.
Availability rule: Towns have permanent shops for most goods, with rare and masterwork goods handled by guild commission.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

entries.biome_identity: canopy markets, covered walkways, medicinal gardens, insect-screen hostels, river skiffs, resin craft shops, and storm shelters.
strict_placement_rules: Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.

Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.

Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

mapping.mapping_note: Mapped to Rainforest because it contains canopy markets, covered walkways, medicinal gardens, river skiffs, resin craft shops, and storm shelters; use vertical treehouse/canopy flavor.

content.summary: Cheap, practical, hearty, local, and generous shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.

content.biome_specific_section_title: Rainforest Biome-Specific Goods and Services
content.full_raw_text:
Village - Rainforest
Source file: Village_Rainforest.html
Cheap, practical, hearty, local, and generous shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: canopy markets, covered walkways, medicinal gardens, insect-screen hostels, river skiffs, resin craft shops, and storm shelters.
Market structure: small common market, hearth inn, livery yard, herb counter, smith stall, and traveling peddlers. Rare luxury goods require ordering through a caravan factor.
Availability rule: Villages list the same categories so the DM has a designated place for every purchase, but rare items are special orders, traveling-stall stock, shrine stock, or one-at-a-time commissions.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

Use these tables as the settlement shopping floor. The same item always has a designated location, so players know where to go and what kind of scene they are entering. Increase or decrease stock by neighborhood, danger rating, scarcity, guild politics, holy days, blockades, monster pressure, or local corruption.

entries.biome_identity: steamship docks, warehouses, seafood markets, ship chandlers, dock taverns, ferry offices, and coastal patrol posts.
strict_placement_rules: Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.

Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.

Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

content.full_raw_text:
Capital City - Surface Docks Coastal
Source file: Capital_City_Surface_Docks_Coastal.html
Prestigious, extravagant, exotic, heavily regulated, and expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: steamship docks, warehouses, seafood markets, ship chandlers, dock taverns, ferry offices, and coastal patrol posts.
Market structure: grand bazaars, embassy hostels, luxury hotels, master guild courts, royal hospitals, relic vaults, and regulated portal offices. Elite purchases include tiny plated courses, rare materials, signed masterwork goods, and private appointments.
Availability rule: Capitals have the broadest stock, elite appointments, rare goods, and strict records for dangerous goods.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office; Skyship Station; Portal Network Building
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

content.full_raw_text:
City - Surface Docks Coastal
Source file: City_Surface_Docks_Coastal.html
Broad, crowded, specialized, fashionable, and more expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: steamship docks, warehouses, seafood markets, ship chandlers, dock taverns, ferry offices, and coastal patrol posts.
Market structure: district markets, guild halls, hotels, armory rows, hospitals, restaurants, bazaars, and licensed arcane counters. Fine goods, rare goods, and commissioned masterwork services are common.
Availability rule: Cities have full permanent districts; almost every listed item can be purchased without waiting unless it is restricted.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office; Skyship Station; Portal Network Building
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

content.full_raw_text:
Town - Surface Docks Coastal
Source file: Town_Surface_Docks_Coastal.html
Fair-priced, varied, reliable, and built for locals plus travelers shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: steamship docks, warehouses, seafood markets, ship chandlers, dock taverns, ferry offices, and coastal patrol posts.
Market structure: town market square, guild street, stable yard, tavern row, clinic, smithy, and craft halls. Luxury goods are available in small batches or by commission.
Availability rule: Towns have permanent shops for most goods, with rare and masterwork goods handled by guild commission.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules

Use these tables as the settlement shopping floor. The same item always has a designated location, so players know where to go and what kind of scene they are entering. Increase or decrease stock by neighborhood, danger rating, scarcity, guild politics, holy days, blockades, monster pressure, or local corruption.
All names are plain English except setting terms such as thundercoil. Merge notes and audit wording have been removed from this player-facing version.

content.biome_specific_section_title: Surface Docks Coastal Biome-Specific Goods and Services
content.full_raw_text:
Village - Surface Docks Coastal
Source file: Village_Surface_Docks_Coastal.html
Cheap, practical, hearty, local, and generous shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: steamship docks, warehouses, seafood markets, ship chandlers, dock taverns, ferry offices, and coastal patrol posts.
Market structure: small common market, hearth inn, livery yard, herb counter, smith stall, and traveling peddlers. Rare luxury goods require ordering through a caravan factor.
Availability rule: Villages list the same categories so the DM has a designated place for every purchase, but rare items are special orders, traveling-stall stock, shrine stock, or one-at-a-time commissions.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

Use these tables as the settlement shopping floor. The same item always has a designated location, so players know where to go and what kind of scene they are entering. Increase or decrease stock by neighborhood, danger rating, scarcity, guild politics, holy days, blockades, monster pressure, or local corruption.
All names are plain English except setting terms such as thundercoil. Merge notes and audit wording have been removed from this player-facing version.

entries.biome_identity: harbor markets, sail lofts, fish halls, inn piers, brine cellars, reef pilots, and ferry yards.
strict_placement_rules: Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.

Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.

Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

content.biome_specific_section_title: Island Biome-Specific Goods and Services
content.full_raw_text:
Capital City - Island
Source file: Capital_City_Island.html
Prestigious, extravagant, exotic, heavily regulated, and expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
Location Profile
Biome identity: harbor markets, sail lofts, fish halls, inn piers, brine cellars, reef pilots, and ferry yards.
Market structure: grand bazaars, embassy hostels, luxury hotels, master guild courts, royal hospitals, relic vaults, and regulated portal offices. Elite purchases include tiny plated courses, rare materials, signed masterwork goods, and private appointments.
Availability rule: Capitals have the broadest stock, elite appointments, rare goods, and strict records for dangerous goods.
Currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
Available location categories: Hostels; Inns; Taverns; Restaurants; Hotels; General Stores; Marketplaces; Armories; Blacksmiths; Craft Shops; Stables; Hospitals; Apothecaries; Alchemists; Magic Item Shops; Jewelers; Furniture Halls; Textile and Clothing Shops; Pet Sellers; Courier and Guild Offices; Housing Office; Skyship Station; Portal Network Building
Meal portions and prices intentionally scale by settlement type: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.
Strict Placement Rules
• Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
• Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
• Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.
• Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
• Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.
• Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
• Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

DM Use Notes
Use these tables as the settlement shopping floor. The same item always has a designated location, so players know where to go and what kind of scene they are entering. Increase or decrease stock by neighborhood, danger rating, scarcity, guild politics, holy days, blockades, monster pressure, or local corruption.
All names are plain English except setting terms such as thundercoil. Merge notes and audit wording have been removed from this player-facing version.

entries.biome_identity: harbor markets, sail lofts, fish halls, inn piers, brine cellars, reef pilots, and ferry yards.
strict_placement_rules: Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.

Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.

Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.

content.summary: Broad, crowded, specialized, fashionable, and more expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.
